explanation: In the United Arab Emirates, eating quietly is a sign of good manners, especially in formal dining settings. Slurping noodles is considered noisy and disrespectful, as it draws attention to the act of eating and may be seen as uncouth. This standard applies across most restaurants, from casual to upscale.
local_tip: Eat noodles silently by twirling them around your fork or spoon, and take small, quiet bites.
regional_note: In more international or tourist-heavy areas like Dubai Marina, some younger or expatriate diners may be more tolerant, but traditional Emirati etiquette still discourages slurping.

also_check.note: Slurping noodles is a compliment to the chef and enhances flavor; it is expected in ramen shops.
Slurping is common and shows enjoyment, though it may be less acceptable in very formal settings.
Slurping pasta is considered very impolite and a breach of table manners.
